title: Renaming/retyping a column on a 900M-row table during a rolling deploy
hidden_flaw: ALTER COLUMN TYPE rewrites the whole 900M-row table under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock (hours of downtime), and dropping/renaming the old column in the same release breaks the old app version that is still serving traffic during the rolling deploy; the change is also non-reversible. Needs expand/contract: add new nullable column, dual-write, backfill in batches, switch reads, then drop in a later release.
notes: Fundamental flaw: table rewrite under lock + destructive change while old code runs.

input.objective: Change orders.amount from INTEGER (cents) to NUMERIC(19,4) and rename it to amount_minor to support currencies with 3-4 decimal minor units.
constraints: Deploys are rolling over ~25 minutes; old and new app versions serve traffic simultaneously.
Rollback of the app must be possible within the release window.
input.context: PostgreSQL 15 primary + 2 replicas. orders has ~900M rows (~410 GB with indexes), ~1,200 writes/s at peak. The app is a Django monolith; migrations run automatically as a pre-deploy job before pods are rolled. Three reporting jobs read orders.amount directly via SQL.
input.proposed_solution: Write a single Django migration: `ALTER TABLE orders ALTER COLUMN amount TYPE NUMERIC(19,4); ALTER TABLE orders RENAME COLUMN amount TO amount_minor;` and update the model and the three reporting queries in the same PR. Run it in the pre-deploy job at night when traffic is lowest. Because it is one transaction, it either fully applies or rolls back, so it is safe.
input.environment: PostgreSQL 15, Django 4.2, Kubernetes rolling deploys, statement_timeout 30s for app role (not for migration role).
